title: Frontend quality gates remain thin: strict TypeScript, browser-level E2E, accessibility and error boundaries are missing

original_titles.title: TypeScript strict mode is disabled for the whole frontend
TypeScript not compiled in strict mode
Frontend test toolchain (Vitest/RTL/Playwright/axe/MSW) absent; one node:test SSR check
No automated axe checks in CI (ACC-03 S2, ACC-01 tracking)
No automated axe checks in CI (and no recorded screen-reader pass)
Frontend coverage: a single SSR XSS test for 6,348 lines of UI
No React error boundary per route or panel
Page conventions unmet: static document title only, no focus-to-heading on route change

problem: CI now runs frontend build and 23 Node-based rendering/logic tests, so the original single-test claim is stale. However tsconfig files do not enable strict mode, test script remains node --test, and there is no Playwright/axe/screen-reader browser suite or route-level React error boundary.
impact: A green TypeScript build does not prove route interaction, keyboard accessibility, cross-browser persistence or error recovery. Strict null/type issues can survive compilation.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Enable strict:true first in the application config, then fix errors in small batches; add noUncheckedIndexedAccess after strict-mode errors are stable.
Add component tests for auth guards, countdown thresholds, offline state, draft conflict, focus restoration, admin role controls and sensitive data hiding.
Add Playwright journeys for participant first sign-in, four-level progression, draft restore, upload/diff submit, reviewer decision and admin correction workflow.
Add axe-core automated checks for main routes and record a short manual keyboard/screen-reader pass for critical flows.
Add route-level error boundaries with retry/reload behavior and capture sanitized diagnostics with request ids.

acceptance_criteria: tsc -b passes with strict mode and no ignored unsafe errors.
Browser E2E covers the core four-level path and admin/reviewer workflows.
Axe CI has no critical/serious violations for required routes.
A rendering/runtime exception is contained to the route/panel and has a recovery path.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.

residual_risk_or_scope_note: CI on the merged PR passed frontend quality and build, but that pipeline does not include the missing Playwright/axe requirements.
